title: Open multiple RMMZ projects on a Mac using Steam

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
I hope this is the right section to post this.
I'm running RMMZ through Steam on a Mac computer. For QOL purposes, I'm trying to open two RMMZ projects at the same time, so I can copy and paste items with more ease. I searched the forum and found a couple older threads that addressed this question, but the solutions no longer seem to work. Google AI Search is also not always reliable but here is what I found.
The Project File Method
You can bypass the RPGMakerMZ app entirely if the program is already running: [
1
]
Have your first project open and running in the editor.
Open
Finder
and locate the folder of your second project.
Find and double-click the
Game.rmmzproject
file inside your second project's folder.
This action will force macOS to spin up a new editor window running that specific project. [
1
,

,

]
Click to expand...
This method no longer seems to work, as it automatically opens the second project in Steam and overrides the first project.
The Terminal Method (If the above fails)
If macOS refuses to open a second instance, you can force it using the built-in terminal: [
1
]
Open
Terminal
(Press Cmd + Space and search for Terminal).
Type the following command and press Enter:
open -n -a /Applications/RPGMakerMZ.app
(Note: Adjust the path if you installed RPG Maker MZ in a custom folder).
Click to expand...
This method also does not work as it gives an error message stating RMMZ is already open.

posts.body:
Not sure why you thought posting (not working) AI responses was in any way, shape or form necessary. You could've just asked the question.
Sadly I'm no apple boy, so I can't test this, but are you positive you can't just open the program multiple times using whatever mac is using instead of the regular .exe file? Not the rmmz project file, the rpg maker exe equivalent.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I poked around a bit, but I think there's basically nothing you can do, short of some kind of sandbox or virtualization
However, you can technically still copy-paste between projects without having them both open at the same time. Obviously it'll be quite a pain, as you need to copy one thing, switch projects, paste that thing, switch projects again, and so on until you're done. But it's doable.
Depending on exactly what you need to copy, there might be an easier way. For example, if it's an entire map, you can just copy the file over in the project folder.
SGHarlekin said:
Sadly I'm no apple boy, so I can't test this, but are you positive you can't just open the program multiple times using whatever mac is using instead of the regular .exe file? Not the rmmz project file, the rpg maker exe equivalent.
Click to expand...
Yeah, that's precisely what the "Terminal method" above is doing (the code isn't quite right – it shouldn't have -a when it's passing the full path to the app – but the general spirit of it is correct). MacOS by default forbids multiple instances of the same app, but the -n flag tells it to override that restriction. The problem is that the app detects another instance of it is already running and just closes.
(For the record, the first method given never would have worked. That's just not how MacOS works.)
